<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step guide for drawing a system design diagram of the NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit, with special emphasis on illustrating how a user interacts via the CLI and how the CLI dispatches to all frontend plugins (console, FastAPI, MCP). Use this as a blueprint and adapt shapes, colors, and layout to your preferred diagramming tool (e.g., draw.io, Visio, Lucidchart).

1. Identify the Project Type and Purpose
   • Type: A modular, framework-agnostic Python toolkit for building, running, profiling, observing, and evaluating “agent” workflows via a CLI and multiple frontend plugins.  
   • Purpose: Provide a unifying API and CLI (“nat” commands) that orchestrates agents, tools, LLM providers, retrievers, memory stores, observability, and evaluation systems.

2. Analyze the File Structure (key directories)
   • src/nat/cli → CLI commands and entrypoint  
   • src/nat/front_ends → Frontend plugins (console, FastAPI, MCP)  
   • src/nat/runtime & src/nat/builder → Core workflow construction and execution  
   • src/nat/agent → Agent implementations (react_agent, reasoning_agent, etc.)  
   • src/nat/llm, src/nat/retriever, src/nat/memory, src/nat/object_store → Pluggable back-ends  
   • src/nat/observability & src/nat/profiler → Telemetry, tracing, profiling  
   • src/nat/eval → Evaluation and benchmarking  

3. Examine README Insights
   • CLI as primary user interface (“nat run”, “nat evaluate”, etc.)  
   • UI chat interface is an optional FastAPI frontend  
   • Plugins for console, MCP client/server, and FastAPI show a plugin pattern  
   • Diagram note in README references a high-level Components Diagram

4. Main Components and Their Interactions
   a. User (CLI)  
      – Initiates commands via shell (`nat run`, `nat evaluate`, `nat info`, etc.)  
   b. CLI Layer (`src/nat/cli`)  
      – Parses commands, flags, config files  
      – Resolves workflows and delegates to:  
         • Frontend plugins (console, HTTP, MCP)  
         • Core runtime engine  
   c. Frontend Plugins (`src/nat/front_ends`)  
      – Console Frontend: Handles interactive console I/O  
      – FastAPI Frontend: Exposes HTTP & WebSocket endpoints + chat UI  
      – MCP Frontend: Exposes/publishes tools over the Model Context Protocol  
   d. Core Runtime & Builder  
      – Builder: Constructs workflows (agents + tools) from YAML/CLI input  
      – Runtime: Loads components, manages sessions, executes workflows  
   e. Workflow Engine  
      – Agents (react_agent, reasoning_agent, etc.) coordinate:  
         • Tool invocations (code execution, document search, external APIs)  
         • LLM calls via providers (OpenAI, NVIDIA NIM, LangChain, etc.)  
      – Retrievers handle embeddings & vector stores (Milvus, NeMo Retriever)  
      – Memory & Object Store for stateful storage (Redis, S3, MySQL)  
   f. Observability & Profiling  
      – Traces, spans, metrics exported to platforms (OpenTelemetry, Phoenix, Weave)  
   g. Evaluation  
      – Built-in evaluators for workflows, RAG, SWE benchmarks  

5. Architectural Patterns and Principles
   • Plugin Pattern: CLI → plugin registry → frontend, LLM, retriever, memory, object store  
   • Separation of Concerns:  
     – CLI layer vs. frontend vs. core runtime vs. back-end adapters  
   • Composition over Inheritance: Workflows composed of small functions/agents/tools  
   • Reactive/Observer Pattern: Internal event streams for intermediate steps & telemetry  

6. Technologies, Frameworks, Libraries
   • Python 3.11+  
   • FastAPI (HTTP/WS frontend)  
   • OpenTelemetry / Phoenix / Weave / Langfuse  
   • Vector stores: Milvus, DataFlywheel  
   • MCP Protocol  
   • Optional frameworks: LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, Google ADK  

7. Diagramming Guidelines
   – Use rectangles for components or modules  (e.g., CLI, Frontends, Runtime).  
   – Use cylinders for storage back-ends (e.g., Redis, S3, MySQL, Milvus).  
   – Use parallelograms for external services (LLM providers, telemetry platforms).  
   – Color-code by layer:  
     • Green: User & CLI  
     • Blue: Frontend plugins  
     • Orange: Core runtime & builder  
     • Purple: Agents & workflow engine  
     • Gray: Back-end adapters & storages  
     • Red: Observability/Evaluation  
   – Label all arrows with data or control flow descriptions (e.g., “command”, “HTTP request”, “workflow config”, “trace/span”).  
   – Show directional arrows:  
     1. User → CLI  
     2. CLI → Frontend Plugin (Console, FastAPI, MCP) & CLI → Core Runtime  
     3. Frontend → Runtime (e.g., WebSocket, REST, MCP wire protocol)  
     4. Runtime → Builder → Workflow → Agents → Tools/LLM/Memory/Store → Agents → Runtime  
     5. Runtime → Observability/Profiler  
     6. Runtime → Evaluation  
     7. Runtime → CLI → User (responses, logs)  

8. Tailoring to This Project & Additional Instruction
   – Emphasize the special flow:  
     User  
       → “nat” CLI entrypoint  
         → dispatch to all available frontends (console, FastAPI, MCP) via plugin registry  
           → frontends orchestrate with the core runtime engine  
   – Clearly show the plugin registry in the CLI layer that dynamically loads:  
     • Authentication providers  
     • Frontend plugins  
     • LLM & retriever & memory & object store adapters  
     • Workflow types  
   – Optionally depict the examples directory as sample configs driving the builder.

9. Final Checklist for Your Diagram
   [ ] Clearly labeled components (CLI, Console FE, FastAPI FE, MCP FE, Runtime, Builder, Agents, Tools, Back-ends, Observability, Evaluation)  
   [ ] Arrows showing user→CLI→(Console, FastAPI, MCP)→Runtime→…→User  
   [ ] Color coding by layer  
   [ ] Shapes to differentiate compute vs. storage vs. external  
   [ ] Plugin registry as central hub in CLI layer  
   [ ] Callouts or annotations for major file paths (e.g., src/nat/cli, src/nat/front_ends)

By following these guidelines and tailoring the diagram to emphasize the CLI’s connections to each frontend plugin, you will produce an accurate, detailed architectural diagram that reflects the NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit’s modular, plugin-driven design.
